explanation: The answer addresses high-temperature stability of high-entropy materials only at a broad thematic level. It does not reconstruct the AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticle system, vacuum heating protocol, temperature-dependent in situ STEM/EDS measurements, or molecular-dynamics analysis. Its central prediction—fine-grained HEAs retaining a homogeneous single phase through entropy stabilization—is contrary to the observed non-sluggish diffusion, Au/Cu surface segregation, shell melting and evaporation, loss of small particles, shape evolution, and approximately 22% size reduction. The proposed coarse-versus-fine-grain comparison is controlled enough to test a grain-size correlation, but it neither separates entropy from grain-boundary effects nor discriminates surface-energy segregation from oxidation mechanisms. Boundaries are qualitative and omit the target's approximately 673 K onset, sub-10 nm size regime, and particle-shape dependence. Consequently, this is not a supported alternative to the target mechanism.
